- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment index (0–1) into forecast by multiplying forecast by (1 + 0.2×sentiment) for bullish sentiment, or (1 - 0.2×sentiment) for bearish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.75 → 0.25 → 0.75), model overfits short-term noise; apply a 3-day smoothing filter to sentiment before weighting.
